name: Zebadiah
overview: Zebadiah was a male Levite who served during the reign of King Jehoshaphat. He is noted in Scripture specifically as a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat, indicating a role of responsibility among the tribe of Levi. No additional personal notes are recorded about him beyond this service.
namesAndTitles: The name Zebadiah means 'Yahweh bestows,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with the faith of Israel. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:8 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Zebadiah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties. Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Zebadiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat, which suggests he was part of the religious reforms and organizational efforts during Jehoshaphat's reign. His involvement underscores the importance of the Levites in supporting the spiritual leadership and worship practices of Israel under God's appointed king.
